draft.title: Series and parallel circuits
card: All the parts are joined one after another on a single path. The charge has only one way to go round.
The parts sit on separate branches. Each branch gives the charge its own path back to the battery.
In a series circuit, a break anywhere opens the one path, so every part stops working. If one globe in a string of series globes breaks, they all go out.
In a parallel circuit, a break in one branch leaves the other branches closed. The globes on those branches keep working. This is one reason houses are wired with parallel circuits.
draft.remember: Series: one path, so one break stops every part. Parallel: separate paths, so the other parts keep working.

a.q: One globe in a circuit breaks and all the other globes go out. How must the globes be connected?
opts: In series, on one shared path
In parallel, each on its own branch
In parallel, but sharing one battery
In series, but each on its own branch
a.why: With one shared path, a break in any globe opens the whole circuit, so every globe stops. In a parallel circuit the other globes would keep working because they have their own branches.
a.clue: Think about how many paths the charge has.

b.q: Priya wires three torch globes to a battery, each on its own branch. One globe burns out. What happens to the other two?
opts: They keep working, as their branches are still closed
They go out, as the circuit now has a break in it
They go out, as the charge must pass through every globe
They keep working, but only because there is one path
b.why: Each globe has its own path to the battery, so a break in one branch does not open the others. The tempting answer is that they go out, which is only true when the globes share one path in series.
b.clue: Each globe is on its own branch.

wants.brief: Two circuit diagrams side by side using standard symbols. Left, labelled Series circuit: a battery and three globes joined in one loop. Right, labelled Parallel circuit: a battery with three globes, each on its own branch between the two sides of the battery.
wants.why: Seeing one path against separate branches makes the difference clear.

a.best: In series, on one shared path

b.best: They keep working, as their branches are still closed
